searchText: Besu devnet6 logs showing a lot of exceptions decoding ENR Response and PING packets - could be that we're not decoding something correctly, or that there's something unexpected in the packets we're receiving - anyone else seeing this or is it just Besu? `2023-06-21 04:24:10.707+00:00 | vert.x-worker-thread-14 | DEBUG | ENRResponsePacketData | Exception Unknown node identity scheme, not defined in record` and `2023-06-22 01:37:03.769+00:00 | vert.x-eventloop-thread-1 | DEBUG | VertxPeerDiscoveryAgent | Discarding invalid peer discovery packet: Malformed packet of type: PING, org.hyperledger.besu.ethereum.p2p.discovery.PeerDiscoveryPacketDecodingException: Malformed packet of type: PING` teku is rate limiting How does one disable rate limit in teku? also teku is giving the same error: thats why chain isn't progressing from teku as well wondering whats the possibility of two clients serving data with similar issue cc <@504202741933932544> make it 3 clients, nimbus as well (the line above the error lists the client name with last segment of peerid, and the error shows the error with the data from the matching peerid) are you seeing the same error from LH again? would be helpful to see logs where we know the peer id of the requesting peer. yes LH gives the same error, just now i added a hack to lodestar<>ethereumjs node to request 2 more slots , and i moved past the problematic epoch , but other lodestar nodes will be stuck in similar fashion let me get the peer id of other stuck nodes (without the hack) for you sorry wrong log wait ```typescript Jun-22 08:04:32.425[network] verbose: Req done method=beacon_blocks_by_range, version=2, encoding=ssz_snappy, client=Lighthouse, peer=16...RGhFwV, requestId=2469 Jun-22 08:04:32.454[sync] verbose: Batch download error id=Finalized, startEpoch=5, status=Downloading Missing blobSidecars for blockSlot=190 with blobKzgCommitmentsLen=6 blobSidecars=4 peerId=16Uiu2HAmA4FsHBWsgpoe8V7es6UnmJ1fi8C6mnGTBoEw29RGhFwV Error: Missing blobSidecars for blockSlot=190 with blobKzgCommitmentsLen=6 blobSidecars=4 peerId=16Uiu2HAmA4FsHBWsgpoe8V7es6UnmJ1fi8C6mnGTBoEw29RGhFwV at matchBlockWithBlobs (file:///usr/app/packages/beacon-node/src/network/reqresp/beaconBlocksMaybeBlobsByRange.ts:90:15) at beaconBlocksMaybeBlobsByRange (file:///usr/app/packages/beacon-node/src/network/reqresp/beaconBlocksMaybeBlobsByRange.ts:46:12) at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:95:5) at wrapError (file:///usr/app/packages/beacon-node/src/util/wrapError.ts:18:32) at SyncChain.sendBatch (file:///usr/app/packages/beacon-node/src/sync/range/chain.ts:399:19) ``` and peer id of the requesting lodestar node: `16Uiu2HAm5sL3Jma8aroSbeaS1BxyjmQucFWKPQphvbFhaydtUBHA` --Xpeer-rate-limit 100000 --Xpeer-request-limit 1000. Defaults are respectively 500 and 50 <@199561711278227457> could you pls apply these to teku nodes? Yup, on it `@all`, feel free to direct testnet updates to me as Barnabas is on vacation 😄 this is strange... i'll look into it.. but if you have the same problem with all clients, whould it possible that the issue is on your side? just asking 🙂 i considered the possibility, but the raw data speaks for itself unless peers send more data, and lodestar decoded less, which could n't be , becuase i did a hack on lodestar<>ethereumjs to request 2 slots more than the 32 slots per epoch which we try to download and lodestar got full data, so lodestar<>ethereumjs is syncing aheead but other lodestar without the hacks are not do you get that consistently? if yes I could to some tracing on our side and see yes for this particular epcoh `5` , for slot `190` this is block by range response this is blobs by range so last slot 190's blobs aren't fully recieved ok i'll look into that. I was assuming as not possible 🙂 its weird that 3 clients will behave in same manner, but i don't understand why the magic number of 4 blobs were received against expected 6 (4 was the max blobs per block last time around) and why the problem went away if i request more count ok if i try to guess: this epoch has 34 blobs, and the blobs by range request count is 32 , so the peers responding with 32 blobs truncating the last 2? and could be reason why increasing `count` resolved the response? so `count` here is being interpreted as blob count instead of slot count? cc <@491624610215886849> <@504202741933932544> ( i have a deja-vu feeling that we have discussed this issue before from may be devnet5/4) no, we consider count as slot count I enabled traces and I see ``` 2023-06-22 10:29:14.483 TRACE - Peer 16Uiu2HAm5sL3Jma8aroSbeaS1BxyjmQucFWKPQphvbFhaydtUBHA requested 32 slots of blob sidecars starting at slot 160. 2023-06-22 10:29:14.570 TRACE - Sent 34 blob sidecars to peer 16Uiu2HAm5sL3Jma8aroSbeaS1BxyjmQucFWKPQphvbFhaydtUBHA. ``` wow ok so may be there is a parsing issue here on lodestar side will debug ok thanks a ton! i have figured out the issue in lodestar, lodestar<>nethermind is now syncing with the in container fix, will update our code
